cards.front: Recall a key point about Exoplanets & Astrobiology
cards.back: An exoplanet is a planet orbiting a star other than the Sun; over 5,500 have been confirmed

cards.front: Recall a key point about Exoplanets & Astrobiology
cards.back: The transit method detects exoplanets by measuring the dip in a star's brightness as a planet passes in front

cards.front: Recall a key point about Exoplanets & Astrobiology
cards.back: The radial velocity (Doppler) method detects the wobble of a star caused by an orbiting planet

cards.front: Recall a key point about Exoplanets & Astrobiology
cards.back: The habitable zone (Goldilocks zone) is the region around a star where liquid water could exist on a planet's surface

cards.front: Recall a key point about Exoplanets & Astrobiology
cards.back: The Drake equation estimates the number of communicative civilisations in the galaxy

cards.front: Recall a key point about Exoplanets & Astrobiology
cards.back: Biosignatures (e.g. oxygen, methane in an atmosphere) could indicate life on exoplanets

cards.front: What should you know about gcse astronomy exam tips — exoplanets & astrobiology?
cards.back: 1. For Exoplanets & Astrobiology questions, define key terms before explaining processes 2. Use 'because' to link cause and effect in your explanations 3. Include units in all calculations and show your working for method marks 4. When evaluating Exoplanets & Astrobiology, consider both the quality of evidence and practical implications 5.
